severityAudit.criteria: Code4rena High/Medium/QA (project CLAUDE.md) + three-law hierarchy (Law-3 footgun reported at HONEST severity, neither auto-capped nor auto-inflated). Independent second opinion; source re-verified at HEAD.
severityAudit.headline: CONFIRM Medium (top-of-band) on M-01. The Plausible-High dissent is a defensible minority view but does not carry: the drain has no attack path against a correctly-configured protocol, the precondition is an owner config state the attacker cannot induce, and — decisively — the literal zero-effort default is NOT a drain. All other severities CONFIRMED.

findings.plausibilitySubTag: Plausible-High is a defensible minority view; primary ruling is Medium (Implausible-High in strict C4 terms because the path is predicated on a partial misconfiguration).

analysis.assetRisk: Confirmed real and machine-verified: in the drain state, 100% of an unconfigured sub-18-dec strategy's skimmed yield is delivered to the claimer for actualPayment==0, permissionless and repeatable. Source re-verified: skimSurplus L484 delivers real underlying; ZeroAmount guard L494 tests the PRE-floor normalized sum (1e9, non-zero) so it does not fire; actualPayment floors at L498/_denormalizeAmount L634; min=0 default disables the L501 guard; safeTransferFrom of 0 succeeds at L509. The asset is in-motion yield owed onward to phlimbo, not SYA principal (SYA holds none).
analysis.attackPath: Valid mechanism, but GATED by an owner config state the attacker can neither create nor induce. addYieldStrategy (L227) and setTokenConfig (L280) are both onlyOwner; nothing an external actor does can move a token into the unconfigured state. Once the state exists the attack is unconditional/deterministic.
analysis.conditions: Owner-side, attacker-uninducible. DECISIVE REFINEMENT (independent deployment-state matrix): the drain requires an ASYMMETRIC partial-misconfiguration — reward token CONFIGURED at <18 dec AND the strategy token left UNCONFIGURED AND that strategy token actually <18 dec. The zero-effort 'nothing configured at all' default is NOT a drain: with both reward and strategy tokens unconfigured, both pass through 1:1 and the errors cancel, so the claimer pays ~fair value (no loss). The drain therefore is NOT 'insecure-by-default' in the literal sense the dissent asserts; it emerges only from a partial config where the reward token was set but a strategy token was forgotten (most plausibly: a strategy added post-launch). This is realistic, but it is a deviation from the protocol's own documented setup (submodule CLAUDE.md lists 'Token Config Mapping — per-token decimals/exchange rate' as a core component and the claim example assumes configured rates), not the expected deployment.
analysis.impact: Severe on trigger (100% yield, permissionless, repeatable, machine-verified via property-4 PoC + halmos SYMBOLIC-001/002), with no hard revert/error signal at config time (preview returns 0 — a soft signal a diligent owner could notice, not a hard one). Symmetric brick variant is fail-safe availability (self-revealing, every claim reverts), clearly not High.

rulingReasoning: C4 High requires a valid attack path WITHOUT hypotheticals against a correctly-configured/correctly-deployed protocol (the canonical Highs — reentrancy, missing access control, accounting underflow — all need no precondition the attacker cannot meet). The no-precondition slice of this bug is EMPTY: a protocol configured per its own documentation is not vulnerable. That alone fails the High bar.

The precondition is an owner config state the attacker cannot induce or control. C4 has consistently capped attacker-uninducible, configuration-gated value-leaks at Medium ('value leak with stated assumptions, but external requirements'). The forgotten setTokenConfig is exactly that stated assumption.

REFUTATION of the dissent's strongest claim ('insecure-by-default for the dominant token type'): the literal default (nothing configured) is NOT a drain — both passthroughs cancel to fair payment. The drain needs the reward token to be DELIBERATELY configured while a strategy token is forgotten. So the vulnerable state is a partial misconfiguration, not the zero-effort default. This materially weakens — and in my independent analysis, defeats — the 'expected deployment' reading that would push it to High.

Law-3 footgun handling is correct: this is a non-obvious footgun (no malice, just a forgotten setter, soft/no signal) so it is IN SCOPE at honest severity — rescued from being dismissed as an invalid 'admin mistake' or auto-capped to Low. 'Honest severity' still applies the C4 likelihood gate, and that gate (attacker-uninducible owner precondition + deviation from documented setup) lands honestly on top-of-band Medium, not High. The footgun rule establishes in-scope-ness and impact-classification, NOT an escalation to High.
correctionsToClassifier: The classifier's 'loss-of-yield (in-motion) Medium ceiling' is a WEAK / secondary justification and must NOT be treated as load-bearing — C4 has no hard rule that all yield loss caps at Medium (directly stealable accrued rewards can be High). The genuine and sufficient cap here is the attacker-uninducible owner-config precondition + empty no-precondition slice. Lean on that, not on yield-vs-principal.

The severityDispute.highArgument overstates the case by calling the vulnerable state 'the DEFAULT a freshly-registered token has.' Accurate framing: the drain needs reward-configured-AND-strategy-unconfigured (asymmetric partial config), which is more specific than the fresh default. Recommend the submission's 'Severity justification' and the 'insecure-by-default' phrasing be tightened to say 'a plausible partial misconfiguration (reward token configured, a strategy token forgotten),' which is both more accurate and a STRONGER defense of the Medium ruling. The PoC caveat already states the reward-token precondition correctly; the prose severity section should match it.
findings.dissentDisposition: Plausible-High DISSENT REVIEWED and NOT SUSTAINED as the primary ruling. It remains a defensible minority view (plausible trigger + total direct impact + soft signal), so it is preserved on the record, but Medium-top-of-band is the correct primary severity. Remediation urgency is unchanged either way — fix is mandatory (fail-closed on unconfigured tokens).
findings.notes: Mechanism independently re-verified against source at HEAD; PoC + halmos corroboration are sound and exercise the real code path. Submission is otherwise accurate and well-scoped (KI#2/#8/#4/#5 distinctions hold; L-01 cross-link correct, do not re-escalate L-01).

analysis.assetRisk: None. No value lost; claim reverts atomically (NudgeNotConfigured L506), NFT preserved, funds unmoved.
analysis.attackPath: No attacker path. Owner-self-inflicted via config ordering (setNudgeSplit(>0) before setNudgeAddress, or clearing nudge while split active). No external party can trigger or sustain it.
analysis.conditions: Owner config-ordering; immediately owner-recoverable by a SINGLE setter.
analysis.impact: Availability gap on the sole core function while the inconsistent state holds — real, but self-inflicted, instantly recoverable, no value loss, atomic.

findings.rulingReasoning: C4 reserves Medium-availability for DoS that an EXTERNAL party can cause, or that is not trivially recoverable, or that locks funds. None applies: the owner both causes and cures it in one tx, no third party is involved, no funds are stuck (yield stays in strategies, NFTs preserved). Above QA because the sole core function genuinely bricks while the window holds and it is a non-obvious write-side enforcement gap (the L506 read-side revert is documented/story-023-faithful; only the missing write-side guard is the bug). Low is correct.
findings.notes: Considered Medium ('core function fully bricked') and rejected: self-inflicted + single-setter-recoverable + no-external-trigger + no-value-loss is the canonical Low availability footgun.

analysis.assetRisk: None. Operational impairment only (consolidation stalls above a gas-vs-incentive threshold; phlimbo stops receiving; preview can revert on gas).
analysis.attackPath: No permissionless trigger. econ-scanner's correction verified against source: addYieldStrategy is onlyOwner (L227) and client growth is via IYieldStrategy.setClient (owner/strategy-owner gated). No external party can force the stall. Self-correcting (owner raises discount / prunes; exemptStrategies mitigates single-strategy pathologies).
analysis.conditions: Owner/strategy-owner-authorized growth past a gas threshold.

findings.rulingReasoning: Static/pattern tools flagged a potential permissionless DoS; econ-scanner authoritatively refuted the premise (both growable dimensions owner-gated), correctly demoting it below the Medium availability bar (no external trigger, owner-recoverable). Root cause is SYA's own loop (in-scope), so KI#7 does not cover it. Low is defensible because there is a genuine non-obvious function-impairment surprise (silent gas-death of the permissionless claim incentive).
findings.notes: This is the WEAKEST of the three Lows and sits squarely on the Low/QA boundary; downgrading to QA would also be defensible. No submission-tier consequence either way — it is already bundled in the QA report. CONFIRM Low as classified.

analysis.assetRisk: None. No protocol value loss and no third-party griefing. econ-scanner verified no profitable sandwich exists (inflating the victim's payment also gifts them discount*donation).
analysis.attackPath: No adversarial path. Two SYA-side slices: (a) min-payment floor only, no max ceiling, so preview-vs-actual divergence can revert the claimer's own approval (self-DoS, NFT preserved, no loss); (b) getTotalYield omits the per-token paused skip that claim()/calculateClaimAmount() apply (view over-reports to integrators).
analysis.conditions: Claimer pre-approves exactly the quote without buffer, or an integrator trusts getTotalYield over the paused-aware path.
analysis.impact: Claimer-side UX self-DoS + integrator view inconsistency.

findings.rulingReasoning: No value leak, no third-party harm — below Medium. Above-or-at QA on the strength of the getTotalYield paused-skip inconsistency being a real correctness slip that can mislead integrators. The two-source preview-vs-actual design itself is documented/story-025-faithful; strategy-side magnitude roots in OOS KI#7. The classifier itself flagged 'near the QA boundary.'
findings.notes: Borderline Low/QA; CONFIRM Low as classified. Downgrade to QA also defensible; no submission-tier consequence (bundled in QA report).

analysis.assetRisk: None beyond the budgeted incentive. The protocol pays exactly discount*yield regardless of who claims — no protocol value leak.
analysis.attackPath: By-design decentralized-conversion incentive (registry designDecisions[0]). The claim race is ordinary MEV; the first claim empties the pot so no shared post-loop balance / sandwich exists. PATTERN-007's nudge winner-take-all signature is a verified red herring (nudge pays a proportional share to an owner-set recipient, L512).
analysis.impact: None (intended); the only residual is the min=0 default note, cross-linked to L-01.

findings.rulingReasoning: No security impact; intended incentive design. Correctly QA/informational, not Low. Kept visible per Law 1 rather than silently dropped.
findings.notes: Correctly NOT escalated to Low — there is no value leak and no exploit.

analysis.attackPath: None. claim() declares `whenNotPaused nonReentrant` (L447); whenNotPaused is a pure storage read of the paused flag with no external call and no state change, so the ordering opens no reentrancy window. Contextual false-positive from a single static source (aderyn).

findings.rulingReasoning: Harmless defensive modifier-ordering note. No security impact. Correctly QA, not Low.
findings.notes: Correct to keep visible as a one-line QA item (Law 1 recall over tidiness).

underStatementCheck.detail: M-01 was the only escalation candidate and is held at Medium with strong, independently-derived reasoning. No other finding has an asset-loss path that is understated. Ledger L-01 is correctly NOT re-escalated (dust-only standalone; M-01 is the amplified, exploitable form). No finding warrants an upgrade.

overStatementCheck.result: No over-statement detected; two Lows are borderline-QA.
overStatementCheck.detail: M-01 is correctly NOT inflated to High despite the severe on-trigger impact — the attacker-uninducible owner precondition (and the fact that the zero-effort default is not even a drain) correctly caps it at Medium. L-05 and L-06 are borderline Low/QA; CONFIRMED as Low but flagged — neither label change has any submission-tier effect since both are bundled in the QA report. L-04 correctly held at Low (not inflated to Medium-availability).

medium: M-01 (top-of-band; Plausible-High dissent reviewed, not sustained as primary)
